Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Qasas (The Stories), because it includes the stories of Musa (peace be upon him) which he related to the elderly man Shu'ayb in the land of Madyan, after he watered the flocks of this elderly man's two daughters, and what followed from his marriage to one of his two daughters.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• A detailed account of the story of Musa, and an explanation of the cause of the collapse of Pharaoh's kingdom. It contains events that make manifest Allah's care for His allies and His forsaking of His enemies in the struggle between truth and falsehood.

• A challenge to the polytheists, concerning the Prophet's ﷺ knowledge of these reports, though he was unlettered: he neither read nor wrote, and did not mix with the People of the Book. It also warns them of the evil consequence of shirk, challenges them with the inimitability of the Qur'an, refutes the excuses they put forward for what would happen if they believed, warns them of what befell the nations that denied before them, and reproaches them for their pride over the Muslims because of their strength and blessings. Those are the enjoyments of this world, whereas what is with Allah for the Muslims is better and more lasting.

• Mention of the cosmic proofs for the oneness of Allah the Exalted, and the blessings He placed in them for His servants, and a reminder to the deniers of what will befall them on the Day of Recompense.

• Presenting as an example for the disbelievers the situation of Qarun among the people of Musa: just as tyranny can arise through rank and authority, it can likewise arise through wealth and property. Qarun's end was destruction and ruin.

• An explanation of the foundations of goodness and happiness in this world and the Hereafter, consolation and steadfastness for the Prophet ﷺ, and a promise that he will return to his homeland and that it will be placed in his control, and that he will be empowered over his enemies.

[Tafsir]

﴿Ta-Sin-Mim﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been given at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 2:**

These are the verses of the Qur'an that I have revealed to you, O Messenger, clarifying everything that the servants need in their worldly life and their Hereafter.
We relate to you, O Muhammad (ﷺ), the true account of Musa and Fir'awn (Pharaoh), for a people who believe in this Qur'an, affirm that it is from Allah, and act upon its guidance.

Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and transgressed, and he made its people into divided factions. He oppressed one group among them, namely the Children of Israel: he slaughtered their sons and spared their women for service and humiliation. Indeed, he was among the corrupters in the land.

Our will was to bestow Our favor upon those who were oppressed by Pharaoh in the land, to make them leaders in goodness and callers to it, and to make them inherit the land after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 6:

We will establish those who were oppressed in the land, and We will show Pharaoh, Haman and their soldiers, at the hands of a boy from the Children of Israel, the very thing from this weak group that they had feared: their destruction, the loss of their dominion, and their expulsion from their homelands.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verses 7–8:

And We inspired the mother of Moses: "Nurse him. But if you fear for him, then cast him into the river, and do not fear [for his safety] nor grieve; We will surely return him to you and make him one of the messengers," [this being] when she gave birth to him and feared that Pharaoh would slaughter him, as he slaughtered the sons of the Children of Israel. So she placed him in a chest and cast it into the Nile, without fear from Pharaoh and his people that they would kill him, and without grief at being separated from him. "Indeed, We will return your son to you and make him one of the messengers." So she placed him in the chest and cast it into the Nile. Then Pharaoh's agents found him and took him up, and the outcome of that was what Allah had decreed: that Moses would become an enemy to them by opposing their religion, and a cause of grief to them through their drowning and the loss of their kingdom at his hand. Indeed, Pharaoh, Haman and their soldiers were sinners and polytheists.

The Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 28, verse 9:

When Pharaoh's wife saw him, Allah placed love for him in her heart, and she said to Pharaoh: "This child will be a source of joy for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." But Pharaoh and his people did not realize that their destruction would come at his hands.

The heart of Musa's mother became empty of everything in the world except concern for Musa and remembrance of him. She came close to revealing that he was her son, had We not strengthened her heart, so she was patient and did not disclose him, so that she would be among the believers who are certain of Allah's promise.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 11:

And Moses' mother said to his sister, when she had cast him into the river: "Follow his trace, and see what is being done with him." So she watched him from afar, while the people of Pharaoh did not realize that she was his sister, and that she was following his news.

And We had forbidden Moses the wet-nurses before that, so his sister said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will raise him for you and nurse him, and they are sincerely concerned for him?" So they agreed to that.

We returned Moses to his mother, so that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve, and so that she would know that the promise of Allah is true. We fulfilled for her His promise: when he returned to her safe from the killing of Pharaoh, and she was not to grieve over his separation from her, and that she would know that the promise of Allah is true regarding what He promised her of returning him to her and making him one of the messengers. Indeed Allah does not break His promise, but most of the polytheists do not know that the promise of Allah is true.

When Moses reached his full strength and his intellect was mature, We gave him wisdom and knowledge, by which he could understand the legal rulings of the Sharia. And just as We rewarded Moses for his obedience and his good conduct, We reward whoever among Our servants does good.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 15:

Musa entered the city while hidden, at a time when its people were unaware. There he found two men fighting: one of them from the people of Musa, from the Children of Israel, and the other from the people of Pharaoh. The one from Musa's people sought Musa's help against the one from his enemies, so Musa struck him with the heel of his palm and he died. When Musa killed him, he said: ﴿This is from the work of Satan﴾, by which he had incited my anger, so that I struck this man and he perished. ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to mankind, a misleader away from the right path, clearly hostile.﴾ This act of Musa, peace be upon him, took place before prophethood.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 16:

Musa said: "My Lord, I have wronged myself by killing the soul that You had not commanded me to kill, so forgive me this sin," and Allah forgave him. Indeed, He is Most Forgiving of the sins of His servants, Most Merciful to them.
Moses said: "My Lord, because of Your favor upon me, granting me repentance, forgiveness, and abundant blessings, I will never be a helper to anyone in his disobedience and crime."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 18:

In the morning, Musa was in Pharaoh's city, fearful and watching for news of what the people were saying about his affair and the affair of the man he had killed. Then he saw the one who had sought his help the day before fighting another Egyptian and asking him for help. Musa said to him: "Indeed, you are a clear misguided one, greatly given to error."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, the simplified tafsir, or Qur'anic exegesis) on Surah 28, verse 19:

When Moses intended to strike the Copt, the man said: "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday? You want nothing but to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not want to be among those who make peace between people."

﴿And a man came running from the farthest part of the city. He said, "O Musa, the nobles of Pharaoh's people are conspiring to kill you, so leave this city. Indeed, I am to you one of the sincere advisers who care for you."﴾
Musa left the city of Pharaoh in fear, awaiting pursuit that might overtake him and seize him, so he prayed to Allah to deliver him from the wrongdoing people.
And when Musa headed toward the land of Madyan and left the dominion of Fir'awn, he said: "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right path to Madyan."

When he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found a group of people watering their livestock there. Apart from that group, he found two women standing alone, away from the people, holding back their sheep from the water, because they were too weak and frail to compete with the men. They were waiting until the people's livestock had left the water, and then they would water their own flock. When Musa (peace be upon him) saw them, he took pity on them and said: "What is your matter?" They said: "We cannot compete with the men, and we do not water [our flock] until the people have finished watering. Our father is an old man who cannot water his flock, because of his weakness and old age."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 24:

So Musa watered their flocks for them, then withdrew to the shade of a tree, sought shelter in it, and said: "My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me, such as food." He had been overcome by severe hunger.

Then one of the two women came to him walking with modesty. She said: "Indeed, my father invites you so that he may give you the reward for having watered [our flock] for us." So Moses went with her to her father. When he came to him and related to him the account of his affair with Pharaoh and his people, her father said to him: "Do not fear; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people," meaning Pharaoh and his people, "for they have no authority in our land."

One of the two women said to her father: "O father, hire him to tend your flock. Indeed, the best one you could hire for herding is the strong one, capable of guarding your flock, the trustworthy one whose betrayal you need not fear in what you entrust to him."

The Shaykh said to Musa: "Indeed, I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me as a hired worker, tending my livestock, for eight years in return. But if you complete ten years, it will be of your own goodness. I do not wish to burden you by making it ten. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous in good companionship and in fulfilling what I have said."

Musa said: "That which you have stated is binding between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfil, I shall have discharged my obligation to you, and I shall not be held to anything beyond it. And Allah is Guardian over what we say: a Trustee who watches over us and knows what we have contracted upon."

When Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) fulfilled the term, the ten years he had agreed to with his father-in-law, which was the more complete of the two terms, and set out with his family towards Egypt, he saw a fire from the side of Mount Tur. Musa said to his family: "Wait and stay here, for I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you news from it, or bring you a burning brand from the fire so that you may warm yourselves by it."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 30–31:

When Moses reached the fire, God called out to him from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the side of the tree: "O Moses, indeed I am God, Lord of the worlds. And throw down your staff." So Moses threw it down, and it became a snake, moving swiftly. When Moses saw it writhing as if it were a jann among the snakes, he turned and fled from it, not even looking back out of fear. Then his Lord called to him: "O Moses, come forward to Me and do not fear; indeed, you are among those who are secure from every harm."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 30–31:

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 32:

Insert your hand into the opening of your garment at the chest, and draw it out, and it will come out white as snow, without any disease or white leprosy. And draw your hand back to your side so that you will be secure from fear. These two, which I have shown you, O Musa, the transformation of the staff into a serpent and the making of your hand white and shining without disease or white leprosy, are two signs from your Lord to Pharaoh and the nobles of his people. Indeed, Pharaoh and his chiefs were a disobedient people.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verses 33–34:

Musa said: "My Lord, I killed a man from the people of Pharaoh, and I fear that they will kill me. My brother Harun is more eloquent in speech than I am, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me, and to explain on my behalf what I address to them. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me in what I say to them: that I have been sent to them."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verses 33–34:

Musa said: "My Lord, I killed a man from the people of Pharaoh, and I fear that they will kill me. My brother Harun is more eloquent in speech than I am, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me, and to explain on my behalf what I address to them. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me in what I say to them: that I have been sent to them."

God said to Moses: "We will strengthen you with your brother, and We will give you both authority (hujjah), so that they cannot reach you with harm. You, O Moses and Harun, and those who follow you, will be the victors over Pharaoh and his people, by means of Our signs and what they point to of the truth."

When Moses came to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our clear signs and proofs bearing witness to the truth of what Moses brought from his Lord, they said: "This is nothing but fabricated magic that you have invented, a lie and falsehood. We have never heard of this that you call us to in our forefathers who passed away before us."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 37:

Arabic text: وقال موسى لفرعون: ربي أعلم بالمحقِّ منّا الذي جاء بالرشاد من عنده، ومَن الذي له العقبى المحمودة في الدار الآخرة، إنه لا يظفر الظالمون بمطلوبهم.

English translation: ﴿And Musa said, "My Lord is most knowing of who has come with guidance from Him and who will have the good outcome in the Home of the Hereafter. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.">﴾

Pharaoh said to the nobles of his people: "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than myself who deserves to be worshipped. So kindle for me, O Haman, a fire upon the clay until it becomes hard, and build for me a lofty tower, so that perhaps I may look upon the god of Moses, whom he worships and calls to worship. Indeed, I think he is among the liars in what he says."

Pharaoh and his soldiers acted arrogantly in the land of Egypt without right, refusing to believe Moses and to follow him in what he called them to, and they thought that after their death they would not be raised again.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 40:

Then We seized Pharaoh and his soldiers, and We cast them all into the sea and drowned them. So look, O Messenger, at how the end of those who wronged themselves and disbelieved in their Lord turned out.

We made Pharaoh and his people leaders leading to the Fire; those who disbelieve and transgress follow their example. On the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. That is because of their disbelief, their denial of the messenger of their Lord, and their persistence in that.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, a simplified exegesis of the Qur'an) on surah 28, verse 42:

And We caused Pharaoh and his people to be followed in this world by disgrace and by wrath from Us upon them. On the Day of Resurrection, they will be among those whose actions are loathsome, those removed from the mercy of Allah.

And We certainly gave Moses the Torah after We had destroyed the earlier peoples—such as the people of Noah, ʿAad, Thamud, the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan (Midian). The Torah was a set of insights (baṣāʾir) for the Children of Israel, through which they could see what benefits and what harms them, and in it was mercy for those among them who acted upon it, so that perhaps they would remember the blessings of God upon them, and thus give Him thanks for them and not be ungrateful.

You, O Messenger, were not on the western side of the mountain when We charged Moses with Our command and prohibition, nor were you among those who witnessed that, so that it could be said that it reached you through this route.

This is the commentary on Q. 28:45 from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the King Fahd Complex's "Simplified Tafsir").

"But We brought into being many generations after Moses, and a long time passed over them, and they forgot the covenant of Allah and abandoned His command. And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan (Midian), reciting Our Book to them, so that you would know their story and report it. But that account you have brought concerning Moses is a revelation, and a witness to your prophethood."

You, O Messenger, were not on the western side of Mount Sinai (Tur) when We called out to Musa, and you did not witness any of that so that you would know it. But We sent you as a mercy from your Lord, so that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, so that they may remember the good you have brought and act upon it, and the evil from which you have forbidden them and so avoid it.

Had it not been that a punishment might befall these disbelievers because of their disbelief in their Lord, and they might say: "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger before this, so that we could follow Your verses revealed in Your Book, and be among those who believe in You."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 48:

When Muhammad came to these people as a warner to them, they said: "Why was this one who was sent to us not given the like of what Moses was given, of tangible miracles, and a Book that was revealed all at once?" Say, O Messenger, to them: "Did they not disbelieve in what Moses was given before? They said: 'The Torah and the Qur'an are two works of magic that support each other in their magic,' and they said: 'We disbelieve in both of them.'"
Say, O Messenger, to these people: "Then bring a Book from Allah that is more upright than the Torah and the Qur'an, and I will follow it, if you are truthful in your claim."

If they do not respond to you by bringing a book, and no argument remains for them, then know that they only follow their own desires. And no one is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah. Indeed, Allah does not guide to the truth the wrongdoing people who have opposed the command of Allah and transgressed His limits.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 51:**

And We have indeed detailed and clarified the Qur'an, O Messenger, as a mercy to your people, so that they may be mindful and take admonition from it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 52:

"Those to whom We gave the Book before it (the Qur'an) — they are the Jews and Christians who did not alter (their scripture) — believe in the Qur'an and in Muhammad (ﷺ)."

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "the Simplified Tafsir") on surah 28, verse 53:**

When this Qur'an is recited to those who were given the Book, they say: "We have believed in it and acted upon what is in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims, monotheists, before its revelation, for the religion of God is one, and it is Islam."

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verses 54–55:

Those whose description has already been mentioned are given their reward twice: for their faith in their own Scripture, and for their faith in the Qur'an, because they were patient. Among their qualities is that they repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them in the way of good and righteousness. When these people hear idle talk, they do not pay heed to it, and they say: "For us are our deeds, and we will not turn away from them; and for you are your deeds, and their burden is upon you. We will not occupy ourselves with replying to you, and you will hear from us nothing but good. We will not address you according to the measure of your ignorance, for we do not desire the way of the ignorant, nor do we love it." This is among the best things that those who call to God say.

This is a commentary on Surah al-Qasas (28), verse 56. The text is from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, published by the King Fahd Complex.

Translation of the passage:

"You, O Messenger, cannot guide by way of divinely granted success (hidayat tawfiq) whomever you love to guide. Rather, that is in the hand of Allah: He guides whomever He wills to guide to faith, and grants him success in it. And He is most knowing of who is fit for guidance, so He guides him."

The unbelievers of Makkah said: "If we follow the guidance you have brought and renounce the protectors and the gods, we will be snatched away from our land through killing, captivity and plunder of our wealth." Did We not establish them in a secure sanctuary, to which the fruits of all things are brought as provision from Us? But most of these polytheists do not know the value of these blessings upon them, so that they would thank the One who bestowed them and obey Him.

This is a commentary passage, not the Qur'anic verse itself, so I translate it as stated:

And many of the people of the towns, We destroyed them when their livelihood distracted them from faith in the Messengers, so they disbelieved and transgressed. Those are their dwellings, which were not inhabited after them except for a little. And it is We who are the inheritors of the earth and whoever is on it; We cause them to die, and then they will return to Us, and We will recompense them for their deeds.

Your Lord, O Messenger, would never destroy the towns around Makkah in your time until He had sent to their mother-town, which is Makkah, a messenger who recites to them Our verses. And We would never destroy towns unless their people were wrongdoers to themselves, through their disbelief in Allah and their disobedience to Him; for this they deserve punishment and retribution.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 60:

Whatever you have been given, O people, of wealth and children, is merely a provision you enjoy in this worldly life and an adornment with which you beautify yourselves. What is with Allah, however, is better and more lasting for those who obey Him and are devoted to Him, because it is everlasting and never runs out. Will you not then have minds, O people, with which you reflect and so distinguish good from evil?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 61:

Is one whom We have promised a good promise, and who will meet what he has been promised, which is Paradise for his obedience to Us, like one whom We have given the enjoyment of the worldly life, its enjoyment, and who then indulges in it and prefers fleeting pleasure over the enduring, and then on the Day of Resurrection will be among those brought forward for reckoning and recompense? The two groups are not equal. Let the intelligent person choose for himself what is more deserving of choosing, which is obedience to Allah and seeking His pleasure.

On the Day when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, calls out to those who associated others with Him in worship, taking the *awliyā'* (those they took as protectors and intercessors) and idols in the world, He will say to them: "Where are My partners that you used to claim were partners to Me?"

Those against whom the punishment has been decreed, who were the callers to disbelief, will say: "Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray. We led them astray just as we ourselves went astray. We disown before You any allegiance to them and any support from them. They were not worshipping us; rather, they were worshipping the devils."

It will be said to the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection: "Call upon your partners whom you used to worship besides God." So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will witness the punishment. Had they been guided to the truth in the world, they would not have been punished.
And [mention] the Day when Allah will call out to these polytheists, saying: "What was your answer to the messengers, concerning what We sent them with to you?"
The proofs were hidden from them, so they did not know what to argue with. They do not ask one another about what they might argue with in the hope of benefiting from the answer.
As for whoever among the polytheists repents, sincerely devotes worship to Allah alone, and acts upon what Allah and His Messenger have commanded him, he is among the successful in both abodes.

Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses whomever He wills among His creatures for His service. No one has any say in the matter or any right to choose; that belongs to Allah alone, glorified be He. He is exalted and far above what they associate with Him.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 69:

﴿And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they reveal.﴾

He is Allah, none has the right to be worshipped except Him. To Him belong the praise and gratitude in this world and the Hereafter, and to Him belongs the judgment among His creation, and to Him you will be returned after your death for reckoning and recompense.

Say, [O Messenger]: "Tell me, [O people]: if Allah were to make the night perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light by which you could see? Will you not then listen with understanding and acceptance?"

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 72:**

Say to them: Tell me, if Allah makes the day perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah who could bring you a night in which you rest and become tranquil? Do you not see with your own eyes the alternation of night and day?

And from His mercy toward you, O people, He made for you the night and the day, alternating between them. He made the night darkness so that you may rest therein and your bodies may be at ease, and He made the day brightness for you so that you may seek your livelihoods therein, and that you may give thanks to Him for His favor upon you in this.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 28, verse 74:**

On the Day when Allah calls out to these polytheists, saying to them: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim in the world were My partners?"

And We will draw out from every nation a witness—and he is their prophet—who will testify to what took place in the world of their polytheism and their denial of their messengers. Then We will say to those nations that denied their messengers and what they brought from Allah: "Bring your proof for what you associated with Allah." Then they will know at that time that the conclusive proof belongs to Allah over them, that the truth belongs to Allah, and that what they used to fabricate against their Lord has vanished from them. But that did not benefit them; rather, it harmed them and led them to the Fire of Hell.

Indeed, Qarun was among the people of Musa (peace be upon him), but he overstepped his bounds in arrogance and in tyrannizing over them. We had given Qarun of the treasures of wealth a great deal, so much that the keys to his storehouses would have been a heavy burden for a large number of strong men. When his people said to him: "Do not exult in what you have of wealth; indeed, Allah does not love those among His creatures who exult, those who do not thank Allah for what He has given them."

Seek, through what Allah has given you of wealth, the reward of the Hereafter, by working in it through obedience to Allah in this world. Do not neglect your share of this world, by enjoying what is lawful in it without extravagance. Be good to people through charity, just as Allah has been good to you with this abundant wealth. Do not seek what Allah has forbidden you, namely corruption on earth and oppression against your people. Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters, and He will recompense them for the evil of their deeds.

Qarun said to his people, who had admonished him: "I have only been given this wealth on account of the knowledge and capability that I possess. Did Qarun not know that God had destroyed before him generations that were stronger than him in might and greater in accumulating wealth?" And the guilty are not asked about their sins, because God already knows them; rather, they are questioned in rebuke and as a confirmation of their guilt, and God punishes them for what He has known of them.

Qarun went out before his people in his finery, intending by that to display his greatness and the abundance of his wealth. When those who desired the adornment of the worldly life saw him, they said: "Would that we had the like of what Qarun has been given of wealth, adornment and standing! Indeed, Qarun possesses a great share of worldly good."

Those who had been given knowledge of God and His law, and who understood the realities of matters, said to those who had said, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given!": "Woe to you! Fear God and obey Him. The reward of God for those who believe in Him and His messengers, and do righteous deeds, is better than what Qarun was given. And none will accept this advice, be granted success in it, and act upon it except those who strive against their own selves, persevere in obedience to their Lord, and avoid His disobedience."
So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. He had no group to support him against Allah, and he was not able to protect himself from Allah when He brought down His punishment upon him.

And those who had wished for his position the day before began to say, in regret and taking warning, fearing that punishment might befall them: "Indeed, Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for whom He wills. Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us up as He did to Qarun. Do you not realize that the disbelievers will not prosper?"

That abode of the Hereafter, We shall assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness over the truth on earth, nor corruption therein. And the praiseworthy outcome, which is Paradise, is for those who fear the punishment of Allah, perform acts of obedience, and abstain from what is forbidden.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 84:

Whoever comes on the Day of Resurrection with sincere monotheism (tawhid) toward Allah and with righteous deeds in accordance with what Allah has legislated, he will have a great reward better than that, and that good is Paradise and everlasting bliss. And whoever comes with evil deeds, those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except according to what they used to do.

Indeed, He who imposed upon you the Qur'an, O Messenger, and obligated you to convey it and to hold fast to it, will surely bring you back to the place from which you departed, which is Makkah. Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists: My Lord knows best who has come with guidance, and who is in manifest error, far from the truth.

And you (O Messenger) did not expect that the Qur'an would be revealed to you, but Allah, glorified and exalted, showed you mercy and revealed it to you. So be thankful to Allah for His blessings, and do not be a helper to the people of polytheism and misguidance.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 28, verse 87:**

Let these polytheists not divert you from conveying the verses of your Lord and His proofs, after He has sent them down to you. Convey the message of your Lord, and do not be among the polytheists in anything.

Do not worship any other deity alongside God; there is no one truly worthy of worship except God. Everything perishes and passes away except His Face. To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned after your death for reckoning and recompense. In this verse is an affirmation of the attribute of the Face for God, the Exalted, as befits His perfection and the greatness of His majesty.
